title: b2b_logic Module
content_markdown:
The B2BUA implementation in OpenSIPS is separated in two layers:

*   a lower one (implemented in the b2b_entities module) - the basic functions of a UAS and UAC
    
*   an upper one (implemented in b2b_logic module) - which represents the logic engine of B2BUA, responsible of actually implementing the B2BUA services using the functions offered by the low level.
    
This module is a B2BUA upper level implementation that can be used along with the b2b_entities module in order to provide various B2BUA services (eg. PBX features). The actual logic of the B2BUA scenarios can be implemented in dedicated script routes.

A B2B session can be triggered in two ways:

*   from the script - at the receipt of an initial INVITE message
*   with an extern command (MI) command - the server will connect two end points in a session(Third Party Call Control).

High Availability for B2B sessions can be achieved by enabling the clustering support offered by the the lower b2b_entities module (by setting the cluster_id modparam from b2b_entities).

how_it_works:
After initializing a B2B session, the call legs will be handled by the b2b_logic module and the first step will be to put the two initial entities in contact. Requests and replies belonging to these dialogs will not enter the script through the standard OpenSIPS routes but instead will be handled in b2b_logic dedicated routes (defined through the script_req_route and script_reply_route modparams or, the custom routes given as parameters to b2b_init_request()). The further steps of the scenario can be implemented in these routes, by calling dedicated b2b_logic script functions in order to perform various actions. Normal "proxy-like" OpenSIPS functions should not be executed in the b2b_logic routes.

Some messages will be handled automatically by the module and will not enter the b2b_logic routes at all (BYE requests received while in the process of bridging two entities, ACKs/BYEs/replies for disconnected entities). Also, if no dedicated b2b_logic reply route is defined, replies will be handled internally by the module, with the same effects as calling b2b_handle_reply() from such a route if it were defined.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash table that stores the session entities.

exported_parameters.name: script_req_route
exported_parameters.description: The name of the script route to be called when requests belonging to an ongoing B2B session are received.

exported_parameters.name: script_reply_route
exported_parameters.description: The name of the script route to be called when replies belonging to an ongoing B2B session are received.

exported_parameters.name: cleanup_period
exported_parameters.description: The time interval at which to search for an hanged b2b context. A session is considered expired if the duration of a session exceeds its defined lifetime. At that moment, BYE is sent in all the dialogs from that context and the context is deleted.

exported_parameters.name: custom_headers_regexp
exported_parameters.description: Regexp to search SIP header by names that should be passed from the dialog of one side to the other side. There are a number of headers that are passed by default. They are: Max-Forwards (it is decreased by 1), Content-Type, Supported, Allow, Proxy-Require, Session-Expires, Min-SE, Require, RSeq. If you wish some other headers to be passed also you should define them by setting this parameter. It can be in forms like "regexp", "/regexp/" and "/regexp/flags". Meaning of the flags is as follows: i - Case insensitive search. e - Use extended regexp.

exported_parameters.name: custom_headers
exported_parameters.description:
A list of SIP header names delimited by ';' that should be passed from the dialog of one side to the other side. There are a number of headers that are passed by default. They are:

*   Max-Forwards (it is decreased by 1)
*   Content-Type
*   Supported
*   Allow
*   Proxy-Require
*   Session-Expires
*   Min-SE
*   Require
*   RSeq

If you wish some other headers to be passed also you should define them by setting this parameter.

exported_parameters.name: cachedb_url
exported_parameters.description: URL of a NoSQL database to be used. Only Redis is supported at the moment.

exported_parameters.name: cachedb_key_prefix
exported_parameters.description: Prefix to use for every key set in the NoSQL database.

exported_parameters.name: update_period
exported_parameters.description: The time interval at which to update the info in database.

exported_parameters.name: max_duration
exported_parameters.description: The maximum duration of a call.
exported_parameters.notes: If you set it to 0, there will be no limitation.

exported_parameters.name: contact_user
exported_parameters.description: If set to 1, adds user from From: header to generated Contact:

exported_parameters.name: b2bl_from_spec_param
exported_parameters.description: The name of the pseudo variable for storing the new “From” header. The PV must be set before calling “b2b\_init\_request”.

exported_parameters.name: server_address
exported_parameters.description: The IP address of the machine that will be used as Contact in the generated messages. This is compulsory only when OpenSIPS starts a call from the middle. For scenarios triggered by received calls, if it is not set, it is constructed dynamically from the socket where the initiating request was received. This socket will be used to send all the requests, replies for that session. This parameter support Pseudo-Variables.

exported_parameters.name: init_callid_hdr
exported_parameters.description: The module offers the possibility to insert the original callid in a header in the generated Invites. If you want this, set this parameter to the name of the header in which to insert the original callid.

exported_parameters.name: db_mode
exported_parameters.description:
The B2B modules have support for the 3 type of database storage

*   NO DB STORAGE - set this parameter to 0
*   WRITE THROUGH (synchronous write in database) - set this parameter to 1
*   WRITE BACK (update in db from time to time) - set this parameter to 2

exported_parameters.name: db_table
exported_parameters.description: Name of the database table to be used

exported_parameters.name: b2bl_th_init_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Call setup timeout for topology hiding scenario.

exported_parameters.name: b2bl_early_update
exported_parameters.description:
Allow bridging of calls in early stage by issuing a "UPDATE" request

*   0 - Do not bridge dialogs in early stage
*   1 - Try to update an session in early stage by sending an UPDATE

exported_functions.name: b2b_init_request

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: identifier for the scenario of this B2B session. The special value top hiding initializes an internal topology hiding scenario. This scenario will do a simple pass-through of messages from one side to another, and no additional scripting or dedicated routes are required.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: CSV list of the following flags

parameters.name: req_route
parameters.description: name of the script route to be called when requests belonging to this B2B session are received. This parameter will override the global script_req_route modparam for this particular B2B session.

parameters.name: reply_route
parameters.description: name of the script route to be called when replies belonging to this B2B session are received. This parameter will override the global script_reply_route modparam for this particular B2B session.

exported_functions.description: This function initializes a new B2B session based on an initial INVITE. A new server entity and a new client entity must be created before running this function, with b2b_server_new() and b2b_client_new(), respectively. These are the initial entities to be connected and further scenario logic can be implemented in the b2b_logic dedicated routes.

exported_functions.name: b2b_server_new

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID used to reference this entity in further B2B actions.

parameters.name: adv_contact
parameters.description: Contact header to advertise in generated messages.

parameters.name: extra_hdrs
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra headers (the header names) to be added for any request sent to this entity.

parameters.name: extra_hdr_bodies
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra header bodies (corresponding to the headers given in the extra_hdrs parameter) to be added for any request sent to this entity.

exported_functions.description: This function creates a new server entity (dialog where OpenSIPS acts as a UAS) to be used for initializing a new B2B session. It should only be used for initial INVITES, before calling b2b_init_request().

exported_functions.name: b2b_client_new

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID used to reference this entity in further B2B actions.

parameters.name: dest_uri
parameters.description: URI of the new destination.

parameters.name: proxy
parameters.description: URI of the outbound proxy to send the INVITE to.

parameters.name: from_dname
parameters.description: Display name to use in the From header.

parameters.name: adv_contact
parameters.description: Contact header to advertise in generated messages.

parameters.name: extra_hdrs
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra headers (the header names) to be added for any request sent to this entity.

parameters.name: extra_hdr_bodies
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra header bodies (corresponding to the headers given in the extra_hdrs parameter) to be added for any request sent to this entity.

exported_functions.description: This function creates a new client entity (dialog where OpenSIPS acts as a UAC) to be used for initializing a new B2B session or for a bridge action. The function can be used before calling b2b_init_request() or b2b_bridge().

exported_functions.name: b2b_bridge

parameters.name: entity1
parameters.description: ID of the first entity to bridge; the special values: peer and this can also be used to refer to existing entities.

parameters.name: entity2
parameters.description: ID of the second entity to bridge; the special values: peer and this can also be used to refer to existing entities.

parameters.name: provmedia_uri
parameters.description: URI of the provisional media server to be connected with the caller while the callee answers.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: CSV list of the following flags

exported_functions.description: This function bridges two entities, in the context of an existing B2B session (the initial entities are already connected). At least one of the two entities has to be a new client entity.

exported_functions.name: b2b_bridge_retry

parameters.name: new_entity
parameters.description: ID of the new entity to bridge.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to retry a failed bridging action by contacting a new destination. A new client entity must be created before running this function with b2b_client_new().

exported_functions.name: b2b_pass_request
exported_functions.description: This function passes a request belonging to an existing B2B session to the peer entity. The function should be called for all requests unless a different action is required to implement the scenario logic (eg. a bridge action).

exported_functions.name: b2b_handle_reply
exported_functions.description: This function processes the received reply by taking the appropriate actions for the current state of the ongoing B2B session (pass reply to peer, send INVITE or ACK to comeplete an ongoing bridge action etc.). The function should be called for all replies, if a b2b_logic reply route is defined.

exported_functions.name: b2b_send_reply

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: reply code

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: reply reason string

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: additional headers

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: message body

exported_functions.description: This function sends a reply to the entity that sent the current request.

exported_functions.name: b2b_delete_entity
exported_functions.description: This function deletes the entity that sent the current request.

exported_functions.name: b2b_end_dlg_leg
exported_functions.description: This function sends a BYE request to the entity that sent the current request. It is not required to also call b2b_delete_entity() in order to delete the current entity.

parameters.name: b2bl_key
parameters.description: a string that contains the b2b_logic key. The key can also be in the form of callid;from-tag;to-tag.

parameters.name: entity_no
parameters.description: an integer that holds the entity of the entity/participant to bridge.

parameters.name: adv_contact
parameters.description: Contact header to advertise in generated messages.

exported_functions.description: This function will bridge an initial INVITE with one of the particapnts from an existing b2b session.

exported_functions.name: b2b_trigger_scenario

parameters.name: scenario
parameters.description: Name of the scenario to be triggered.

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Parameters to be used in this scenario (optionally as CSV). Flags: n (Enable rfc3515 NOTIFY), session key (Internal session key), party of remote session (0 = A-Party, 1 = B-Party).

parameters.name: peer1
parameters.description: Parameters to define the A-Party of the triggered scenario (entity_name, RURI, Proxy, Display-Name).

parameters.name: extra_headers_peer1
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra headers (the header names) to be added for any request sent for the first entity.

parameters.name: extra_headers_contents_peer1
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra header bodies (corresponding to the headers given in the extra_headers_peer1 parameter) to be added for any request sent for the first entity.

parameters.name: peer2
parameters.description: Parameters to define the B-Party of the triggered scenario. The format is identitical to the definition of peer1.

parameters.name: extra_headers_peer2
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra headers (the header names) to be added for any request sent for the second entity.

parameters.name: extra_headers_contents_peer2
parameters.description: AVP variable holding a list of extra header bodies (corresponding to the headers given in the extra_headers_peer2 parameter) to be added for any request sent for the second entity.

exported_functions.description: This function triggers a certain scenario from routing script, e.g. out-of-dialog REFERs.

exported_mi_functions.name: b2b_trigger_scenario

parameters.name: senario_id
parameters.description: ID for the scenario of this B2B session.

parameters.name: entity1
parameters.description: first entity to be connected; specified in the following format: id,dest_uri[,from_dname] where: id - ID used to reference this entity in further B2B actions; dest_uri - URI of the new destination; from_dname (optional) - Display name to use in the From header.

parameters.name: entity2
parameters.description: second entity to be connected; specified in the same format as entity1

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: array of B2B context values, in the format: key=value

exported_mi_functions.description: This command initializes a new B2B session where OpenSIPS will start a call from the middle. The initial entities to be connected are specified through the command's parameters and further scenario logic can be implemented in the b2b_logic dedicated routes.

examples.code: opensips-cli -x mi b2b_trigger_scenario marketing client1,sip:bob@opensips.org client2,sip:322@opensips.org:5070 agent_uri=sip:alice@opensips.org

exported_mi_functions.name: b2b_bridge

parameters.name: dialog_id
parameters.description: the b2b_logic key, or the callid;from-tag;to-tag of the ongoing dialog.

parameters.name: new_uri
parameters.description: the uri of the new destination

parameters.name: flag
parameters.description: used to specify that the callee must be bridged to the new destination. If not present the caller will be bridged. Possible values are '0' or '1'.

parameters.name: prov_media_uri
parameters.description: the uri of a media server able to play provisional media starting from the beginning of the bridging scenario to the end of it. It is optional. If not present, no other entity will be envolved in the bridging scenario

exported_mi_functions.description: This command can be used by an external application to tell B2BUA to bridge a call party from an on going dialog to another destination. By default the caller is bridged to the new uri and BYE is set to the callee. You can instead bridge the callee if you send 1 as the third parameter.

exported_mi_functions.name: b2b_list
exported_mi_functions.description: This command can be used to list the internals of b2b_logic entities.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: the b2b_logic key or the callid;from-tag;to-tag of one of call legs of the ongoing session.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $b2b_logic.key
exported_pseudo_variables.scope: request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules
exported_pseudo_variables.description:
This is a read-only variable that returns the b2b_logic key of the ongoing B2B session.

The variable can be used in request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $b2b_logic.entity(field)[idx]
exported_pseudo_variables.scope: request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules
exported_pseudo_variables.description:
This is a read-only variable that returns information about the entities(dialogs) involved in the ongoing B2B session.

The available entity information is:

*   the Call-ID of the dialog, accessible by using the callid subname;
    
*   the entity key, accessible by using the key subname or no subname at all.
    
*   the entity ID, accessible by using the id subname.
    
*   the From-Tag of the dialog, accessible by using the fromtag subname.
    
*   the To-Tag of the dialog, accessible by using the totag subname.
    

The index is used to select which entity from the B2B session to refer to. The only possible values are 0 or 1 and correspond to the positions of the entities in the scenario. Initially, this depends on the order in which the entities are created. In the case of the internal topology hiding scenario, 0 is the caller and 1 is the callee. When a further bridge action happens, the bridged entity is always placed on the 0 index and the new entity on 1.

If no index is provided, the variable will refer to the entity(dialog) which the current SIP message belongs to.

The variable can be used in request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $b2b_logic.ctx(key)
exported_pseudo_variables.scope: request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules
exported_pseudo_variables.description:
This is a read-write variable that provides access to a custom Key-Value storage(of string values) in the context of the ongoing B2B session.

The variable can be used in request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules. In the main request route the variable can be used for storing a new context value even before instantiating the scenario with b2b_init_request().

Setting the variable to NULL will delete the value at the given key.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $b2b_logic.scenario(key)
exported_pseudo_variables.scope: request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules
exported_pseudo_variables.description:
This is a read-only variable that returns the scenario ID of the ongoing B2B session

The variable can be used in request route, local_route and the dedicated routes defined through the b2b_entities and b2b_logic modules.
